purpose: Compare deterministic checker alert burden across v1.1/v1.2/v1.3 candidate and identify signals to disable or weaken. Not a generative Skill A/B.

retained_positive_control.note: Candidate aggregates repeated hype into one density finding instead of one finding per lexical hit.

evidence_based_changes.reason: Pilot alerts occurred in published news/native technical prose without demonstrated editorial value.
Pilot alert occurred in technical instructions; feature retained for future corpus analysis.
Legitimate technical/factual uses of бесшовный and флагманский produced lexical false positives.
Technical and official contexts can use these lexemes descriptively/terminologically.

limitations: Small pilot: 15 documents / 1842 words; not representative of all Russian.
No real social, fiction, L2, accessibility, product-case or long legal documents in this pilot.
RuCoLA unacceptable sentences are diagnostic only; checker is not a grammar classifier.
No independent generative model trials were run; results apply to deterministic check_prose_ru.py only.
Alert burden on published text is not identical to false-positive rate; only contextually reviewed cases can be labelled false positives.

comparison.interpretation: Reduction in emitted checker findings on this pilot, not a measured reduction in language errors and not a full false-positive rate.
